Several software firms now sell "vibe coding cleanup" services, which take AI-built prototypes and turn them into production-ready software. Most offer some mix of audit, refactoring, security hardening, and testing.

- **Innowise** offers audits, refactoring, security hardening, QA automation, performance work, and CI/CD with monitoring. Its audit maps the app's weak spots and sets cleanup priorities. (Vibe coding cleanup services take a working prototype to production-ready software.)
- **Chudovo** runs a four-step process: a free codebase assessment (1–3 days), a cleanup roadmap with cost estimates, cleanup execution (2–4 weeks), and handover with ongoing support. (The engineering team provides a free codebase evaluation, identifying the main problem areas and outlining technical issues and vulnerabilities.)
- **Softteco** focuses on audits, refactoring, and building automated test suites, and says it can align systems with regulations such as GDPR and HIPAA. (Its engineers establish automated testing that includes unit, integration, and end-to-end tests.)
- **Acropolium** says it can clean up code while the product stays live, and sometimes recommends a full rebuild when that's cheaper. (It audits, hardens, and tests vibe-coded builds, rebuilding them entirely when that's the cheaper answer.)
- **DBB Software** targets funded startups and solo founders with AI-built MVPs, and it advertises AWS partner status and a 5.0 rating on Clutch. (It positions itself as a way to move a vibe-coded app from a fragile AI prototype to production-ready infrastructure.)
- **Redwerk** frames its offering as a peer review plus refactoring process. (Its service is a professional peer review and refactoring process.)

The vendors' statistics about AI-generated code, such as the claim that 62% of it is flawed or vulnerable, come from their own marketing pages and cite third-party sources I didn't verify. Treat those numbers with caution. Pricing wasn't listed on any of the pages, so you'd need to request a quote from each vendor.

"Vibe code rescue" is a real niche. Several agencies advertise services for AI-generated apps that break once real users arrive. The results are mostly vendor marketing, so the claims are unverified.

- **MetaCTO (Vibe Rescue):** Offers a free 48-hour code audit, then a plan to take the app to production in about 30 days. Its listed fixes include replacing hallucinated library calls, rebuilding auth, and adding tests and CI. It targets founders who built prototypes with tools like Cursor, Lovable, or Bolt.
- **Rocking Tech (UK):** Runs a three-phase "Platform Rescue" process. It starts with a free 30-minute code health assessment, then a fixed-price discovery sprint, then an optional rebuild. The sprint fee is credited toward the rebuild.
- **Wavect (Austria):** Offers a closed-scope code audit and a full rescue service. Its page is in Spanish and cites a Veracode figure that 45% of AI-generated code introduces a security vulnerability.
- **Pragmatic Coders (Kraków):** Has a Vibe Coding Rescue service line, starting with a free first consultation.
- **Other names in directories:** Beesoul (free audit), Varyence (security assessments), Railsware, ISHIR, and Hey Ferrante. These come from a vibecoding.app listing, which says audits range from free to about $6k.

Some of these details come from agencies' own pages, and the directory rankings may be paid placements. Check pricing and track records directly before hiring.

The quoted line is the launch pitch for **Slopfix**, a three-engineer team. It appeared on Hacker News in July 2026 and was picked up by several outlets.

- **The offer:** Slopfix charges a flat $10,000 for one week of refactoring. It is paid according to how much code it deletes. Before starting, the engineers agree to a line-reduction target, with an example of cutting a 100,000-line project to 35,000 while keeping the same functionality.
- **The method:** Slopfix uses AI coding agents itself. It begins with a written inventory of the application, screen by screen and endpoint by endpoint, which doubles as a regression checklist. The founder says the agent is kept on a very short leash.
- **Guarantees:** A two-week warranty covers issues arising from a previously working component. Slopfix analyzes client repos for free and walks away if it decides it can't make a meaningful difference.

A separate WebProNews article describes a $10K/week service called "Pull" that does something similar. I'd treat that one with caution. Its claims are less specific and it doesn't match the Slopfix details that multiple other sources report, so it may be a confused or unreliable write-up.
